replacement_title: Damron-Hanson-Houdré-Xu 2019: planar quantile separation and logarithmic variance consequence
replacement_statement: For iid nonnegative nearest-neighbor edge weights on Z^2, let I=inf supp(F). Under F(0)<p_c(2) and, when I>0, F(I)<the two-dimensional oriented bond threshold, arXiv:1810.08270v2 Theorem 1 provides two positive-probability quantiles of T(0,x) separated by c sqrt(log ||x||) for all sufficiently large ||x||. The sharp two-quantile variance inequality then gives Var(T(0,x))>=c' log ||x|| whenever T(0,x) is square-integrable. The paper's d>2 discussion gives only constant-scale fluctuation lower bounds by this method; its higher-dimensional extension is for thin cylinders under an extra moment assumption. These results do not establish a positive power-law fluctuation exponent or chi=1/3.
proof_of_variance_consequence: If P(X<=a)>=p and P(X>=b)>=q for a<b, then Var(X)>=pq(b-a)^2/(p+q) by minimizing the two tail contributions to E(X-EX)^2. Apply with b-a>=c sqrt(log ||x||).
